subject: Post-call recap: residency & retention checklist for prompt outputs
messages:
From: Lucas Jenkins <lucas.jenkins@clearviewhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@clearviewhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from demo — residency & retention clarifications

Hannah,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the team appreciated the latency numbers and the multi-region routing examples. A couple of compliance items came up in our security review and I wanted to capture them explicitly so we can move to a procurement timeline: 

- For prompt inputs and model outputs, what is Redwood's default retention period for hosted API customers? Does that differ for Dedicated or Private deployments?
- Can you confirm whether prompt outputs that contain patient identifiers (our PII class) are ever written to disk in hosted mode, or are they strictly only in-memory/KV cache?
- Residency: we need to ensure outputs and associated telemetry for the CVH environment remain in the US (no EU/ASIA copies). Are there automated cross-region backups for logs/metrics we should worry about?

If you can put a short checklist of what you store, where it lives, and the default retention window, that will help our InfoSec signoff.

Attaching our high-level security questionnaire for context (we'll be more specific on the SOC2 artifacts in a follow-up).

Best,
Lucas
Senior Security Manager
ClearView Health

[Attachment: CVH_security_questionnaire_v1.docx]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Jenkins <lucas.jenkins@clearviewhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@clearviewhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — residency & retention clarifications

Lucas — thanks for the clear list. Per our call I wanted to summarize the answers and next steps so your procurement and InfoSec teams have something to review quickly. See bullets below; I'm also looping Aditya for pricing/contract impacts and Marissa for the SOC2/evidence items.

Short answers (full detail below):
- Default hosted retention for prompt inputs/outputs: 30 days (configurable).
- Dedicated: customer can opt for zero retention (ephemeral only) or set a custom retention policy as part of the reserved capacity contract.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): retention and storage are fully customer-controlled — Redwood control plane can be configured not to persist outputs.
- On-disk writes: in hosted mode, outputs may be persisted to our encrypted object store for caching and replay (default 30d). Sensitive fields (PII classes you highlighted) can be redacted or dropped via a field-mapping policy; we can also enable an opt-in ‘no-persistence’ flag for your account.
- Residency: customer-level tenant placement determines where primary storage lives. For US-only commitment we can pin data to our us-west/us-east regions; we do not replicate prompt outputs to EU/APAC unless requested. Operational metrics that are aggregated at service level are US-resident when the tenant is pinned to US.

Concrete deliverables I will provide today:
1) A one-page table that enumerates what is stored (inputs, outputs, KV cache, audit logs, metrics), the storage location, and default retention — I'll attach as CSV.
2) SOC2 artifacts and a brief on how we encrypt data at rest and in transit (Marissa will share the SOC2 summary and the audit contact).
3) A configuration checklist for a Dedicated reservation or Private deployment that enforces zero-persistence.

Open question for your team: do you need per-field redaction (e.g., remove MRN / SSN fields from stored outputs) or would account-level no-persistence suffice? If per-field redaction, we'll propose a small mapping policy and a verification test.

Next steps: Aditya to propose the commercial path (Dedicated vs Hosted with no-persistence add-on) with pricing; Marissa to send SOC2 package; I'll push the CSV residency/retention table by EOD.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood-residency-table.csv)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Jenkins <lucas.jenkins@clearviewhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@clearviewhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — residency & retention clarifications

Lucas / Priya — adding a few practical notes from the commercial side so you can map to procurement timelines: 

- Hosted default (30d) is what most PLG customers keep; we can change tenant policy prior to go-live but it is a config change that affects caching and debugging ability. If you require zero-persistence for outputs we recommend Dedicated or Private (Dedicated can be contracted with zero-persistence SLA).
- Pricing delta: zero-persistence on Hosted (account-level opt-out) carries a small monthly surcharge because we remove caching optimizations; Dedicated (reserved GPUs) provides predictable unit costs and can include zero-persistence with standard reserved-capacity pricing. I'll follow up with a short commercial comparison doc and numbers.
- Verification/testing: we can run a pre-prod test (one-week run) with a synthetic prompt set that contains flagged PII fields; we'll show logs and storage headers and provide a signed statement of the observed retention behavior. This is commonly used for procurement evidence.

I'll prepare: commercial comparison, a one-week verification test plan, and contract language snippets for the data residency/retention clause.

—Aditya
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

[Attachment: commercial-comparison-draft.docx]

From: Lucas Jenkins <lucas.jenkins@clearviewhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@clearviewhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — residency & retention clarifications

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two quick confirmations before I circulate to InfoSec: 

1) Can you confirm the exact storage class/location for hosted outputs when tenant is pinned to US-west? We need region/cluster identifiers to map into our procurement data flow (e.g., us-west-2, s3 bucket name pattern).
2) For the verification test: can Redwood provide an exported manifest at the end of the week that shows object keys and timestamps (redacted content OK) so we can validate deletion timelines?

If you can confirm those two items in a short note and attach the CSV you mentioned, I'll share with our procurement lead and aim to lock commercial terms next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Lucas
Senior Security Manager
ClearView Health
